
```{r}
library(adempR)
```

This vignette describes the analyses that go beyond the standard table
of performance measures: functional and categorical estimands, scoring
rules, checks of the truth and of known performance, rankings, verdicts
against acceptable ranges, the influence of design factors, anytime
valid monitoring, adaptive allocation, analyses of very large runs,
simulation based calibration, tuning of method settings, blinded
external analysis, and the tools that manage a study and its runs.

A small study is used throughout.

```{r}
study <- sim_study("demo", scenarios = sim_scenarios(n = c(10L, 40L), sd = c(1, 3)),
  generate = function(scenario, context) rnorm(scenario$n, 0, scenario$sd),
  estimands = list(sim_estimand("mean", sim_truth_exact(function(scenario) 0))),
  methods = list(
    mean = function(data) {
      tt <- t.test(data)
      sim_estimate("mean", mean(data), se = sd(data) / sqrt(length(data)),
                   lower = tt$conf.int[1], upper = tt$conf.int[2], level = 0.95,
                   p_value = tt$p.value, null = 0)
    },
    median = function(data) sim_estimate("mean", median(data))),
  measures = c("bias", "empse", "mse", "coverage", "rejection"))
run <- sim_run(study, replications = 60, seed = 1, path = tempfile("adempR-run-"))
```

`sim_summarize()` is an alias of `sim_summarise()`.

```{r}
s <- as.data.frame(sim_summarize(run, measures = "bias"))
s[s$measure == "bias", c("scenario_id", "method", "value", "mcse")]
```

## Curves and other functionals on a grid

An estimand defined on a grid of points (a survival curve, a dose
response, a quantile function) is declared with `sim_estimand_grid()`;
methods return all points with `sim_estimate_grid()`, and
`sim_summarise_grid()` gives each measure per point together with its
average over the grid. Every point keeps its own eligibility and status:
an infinite estimate at one point is reported, not dropped.

```{r}
grid <- c(0.5, 1, 2)
curve <- sim_study("curve", scenarios = sim_scenarios(n = 100L, rate = 0.5),
  generate = function(scenario, context) rexp(scenario$n, scenario$rate),
  estimands = sim_estimand_grid("surv", grid,
    truth = function(scenario, at) exp(-scenario$rate * at)),
  methods = list(empirical = function(data) {
    sim_estimate_grid("surv", grid, vapply(grid, function(t) mean(data > t), numeric(1)))
  }))
run_curve <- sim_run(curve, replications = 30, seed = 1, path = tempfile("adempR-run-"))
sim_summarise_grid(run_curve, "surv", "bias")
```

## Categorical estimands

An estimand of type `"categorical"` is a class coded as a number, such as
a selected model. `sim_measures_categorical()` gives the proportion of
correct selections, the proportion choosing each declared class, and
the proportion of outputs outside the declared classes, each with an
exact interval.

```{r}
select <- sim_study("select", scenarios = sim_scenarios(n = c(20L, 200L)),
  generate = function(scenario, context) rnorm(scenario$n, 0.3),
  estimands = list(sim_estimand("model", type = "categorical",
                                truth = sim_truth_exact(function(scenario) 2))),
  methods = list(test = function(data) {
    sim_estimate("model", if (t.test(data)$p.value < 0.05) 2 else 1)
  }),
  measures = sim_measures("usable", sim_measures_categorical(1:2, c("null", "alt"))))
run_select <- sim_run(select, replications = 40, seed = 1, path = tempfile("adempR-run-"))
s <- as.data.frame(sim_summarise(run_select))
s[s$measure != "usable", c("scenario_id", "measure", "value", "lower", "upper")]
```

## Interval score

The interval score of Gneiting and Raftery rewards narrow intervals and
penalizes misses in proportion to their distance; lower is better. Pass
it to `sim_measures()` with other measures.

```{r}
scored <- sim_study("scored", scenarios = study$scenarios, generate = study$generator,
  estimands = study$estimands, methods = study$methods["mean"],
  measures = sim_measures("coverage", sim_measure_interval_score()))
run_scored <- sim_run(scored, replications = 40, seed = 1, path = tempfile("adempR-run-"))
s <- as.data.frame(sim_summarise(run_scored))
s[s$measure == "interval_score", c("scenario_id", "value", "mcse")]
```

## Decomposing bias against another reference

`sim_bias_decomposition()` splits the bias against the declared truth
into the bias against another reference (what the method actually
estimates) and the difference between the two references. Here the
sample mean of log normal data is consistent for the population mean,
not for the median that was declared as the truth.

```{r}
lognormal <- sim_study("lognormal", scenarios = sim_scenarios(n = 50L, mu = 0),
  generate = function(scenario, context) exp(rnorm(scenario$n, scenario$mu)),
  estimands = list(sim_estimand("median", sim_truth_exact(function(scenario) exp(scenario$mu)))),
  methods = list(mean = function(data) sim_estimate("median", mean(data))))
run_ln <- sim_run(lognormal, replications = 100, seed = 1, path = tempfile("adempR-run-"))
sim_bias_decomposition(run_ln, function(scenario) exp(scenario$mu + 0.5),
                       label = "population mean")
```

## Identities between estimands

When estimands are linked by an identity (here the log of one is the
other), `sim_check_identity()` checks it on the truths or on the
estimates of every replication. The tolerance is stated in the units of
the residual; `scale` turns it into a relative tolerance (a number, or a
function of the inputs), and a numerical truth's stated error bound is
added to the allowed residual.

```{r}
ratio <- sim_study("ratio", scenarios = sim_scenarios(n = 40L, mu = 1),
  generate = function(scenario, context) rexp(scenario$n, 1 / scenario$mu),
  estimands = list(
    sim_estimand("mean", sim_truth_exact(function(scenario) scenario$mu)),
    sim_estimand("log_mean", sim_truth_exact(function(scenario) log(scenario$mu)))),
  methods = list(mle = function(data) list(sim_estimate("mean", mean(data)),
                                        sim_estimate("log_mean", log(mean(data))))))
run_ratio <- sim_run(ratio, replications = 20, seed = 1, path = tempfile("adempR-run-"))
id <- sim_check_identity(run_ratio, function(mean, log_mean) log(mean) - log_mean,
                         target = "estimate")
head(id[, c("replication", "residual", "allowed", "status")], 3)
```

## Known performance as a check

A method whose performance is known from theory can declare it with
`sim_method(reference = )`. `sim_check_reference()`, also run by
`sim_diagnose()`, flags cells where the estimate disagrees beyond Monte
Carlo error, which points to a bug in the generator, the truth or the
evaluation. With antithetic pairs the check uses the pairs.

```{r}
checked <- sim_study("checked", scenarios = sim_scenarios(n = 20L),
  generate = function(scenario, context) rnorm(scenario$n),
  estimands = list(sim_estimand("mean", sim_truth_exact(function(scenario) 0))),
  methods = list(mean = sim_method(function(data) {
    tt <- t.test(data)
    sim_estimate("mean", mean(data), lower = tt$conf.int[1], upper = tt$conf.int[2], level = 0.95)
  }, reference = c(bias = 0, coverage = 0.95))),
  measures = c("bias", "coverage"))
run_checked <- sim_run(checked, replications = 100, seed = 1, path = tempfile("adempR-run-"))
sim_check_reference(run_checked)
```

## Ranking methods

`sim_rank()` ranks methods per scenario on the replications where all of
them have a usable result, with a paired bootstrap for the probability
of first place and the mean rank. The bootstrap holds the truth fixed;
when the truth is a Monte Carlo or numerical approximation, the output
says so (`truth_conditional`, `truth_halfwidth`) and shifts the truth,
which every method shares, jointly over its error range. A cell whose
first place changes within that range gets status `truth_sensitive`.

```{r}
rk <- sim_rank(run, "mse", B = 200)
rk[, c("scenario_id", "method", "rank", "p_first", "truth_conditional", "status")]
```

## Verdicts against an acceptable range

`sim_acceptable()` classifies each cell as `inside`, `outside` or
`uncertain` relative to an acceptable range, taking the Monte Carlo
interval into account. For the rejection rate under the null the default
is Bradley's liberal criterion.

```{r}
sim_acceptable(run, "rejection")[, c("scenario_id", "method", "value", "verdict")]
```

## Influence of design factors

`sim_factor_influence()` fits a weighted metamodel of a measure on the
scenario factors and reports how much of the variation between
scenarios each factor explains. Exclusions are applied first; a factor
that no longer varies among the remaining cells is reported as dropped.

```{r}
sim_factor_influence(run, "empse", method = "mean")
```

## Monitoring with confidence sequences

A confidence sequence is valid at every number of replications at once,
so a run can be looked at repeatedly and stopped at any time. The tuning
is recorded in the run at the first call and reused afterwards. A Monte
Carlo truth, or a numerical truth with a nonzero error bound, is refused
for coverage and MSE, since the guarantee would hold only for the
approximate reference value.

```{r}
cs <- sim_confidence_sequence(run, "coverage")
cs[, c("scenario_id", "method", "n", "estimate", "lower", "upper", "type")]
```

## Adaptive allocation of replications

`sim_run_adaptive()` runs a pilot, estimates the replications each
scenario needs for a target MCSE, and adds them in rounds up to a cap.
Each scenario keeps its own random number streams, so the result is
the same as a run with those numbers of replications.

```{r}
adaptive <- sim_run_adaptive(study, "bias", target = 0.1, seed = 1,
                             path = tempfile("adempR-run-"), initial = 20,
                             max_replications = 200)
adaptive$allocation
```

## Very large runs

`sim_summarise_stream()` reads one committed batch at a time and
accumulates the moments each measure needs, so memory does not grow with
the size of the stored results. Values, MCSEs and statuses agree with
`sim_summarise()` up to rounding.

```{r}
st <- sim_summarise_stream(run, measures = c("bias", "empse"))
head(as.data.frame(st)[, c("scenario_id", "method", "measure", "value", "mcse")])
```

Scenarios can also be split across machines. `sim_shard_scenarios()`
says which scenarios a shard owns, `sim_run_shard()` runs them, and
`sim_collect_shards()` merges the shards into one run after checking
that they belong to the same study and seed.

```{r}
sim_shard_scenarios(study, shard = 1, n_shards = 2)
parent <- tempfile("adempR-shards-")
for (k in 1:2) sim_run_shard(study, k, 2, replications = 10, seed = 1, path = parent)
merged <- sim_collect_shards(study, 2, replications = 10, seed = 1, path = parent,
                             into = tempfile("adempR-run-"))
```

## Simulation based calibration

For a Bayesian method, `sim_method_sbc()` wraps a function returning
posterior draws: the estimate is the posterior mean, the interval a
central credible interval, and the rank of the truth among the draws is
stored. With a data set truth drawn from the prior, `sim_sbc()` tests
that the ranks are uniform in every scenario.

```{r}
sbc <- sim_study("sbc", scenarios = sim_scenarios(n = 10L),
  generate = function(scenario, context) {
    mu <- rnorm(1)
    sim_data(rnorm(scenario$n, mu), truth = list(mu = mu))
  },
  estimands = list(sim_estimand("mu", sim_truth_dataset())),
  methods = list(exact = sim_method_sbc(function(data) {
    n <- length(data)
    rnorm(200, sum(data) / (n + 1), sqrt(1 / (n + 1)))
  }, "mu")))
run_sbc <- sim_run(sbc, replications = 60, seed = 1, path = tempfile("adempR-run-"))
sim_sbc(run_sbc, "exact")
```

## Tuning method settings on separate streams

Choosing a tuning parameter on the data used for evaluation favors it.
`sim_calibrate_method()` evaluates a grid of settings on data drawn from
a separate stream family, so the production run never sees the data used
for tuning. Scenarios with zero weight, or where no setting has a loss,
are left out and named; when nothing is left the call is an error
instead of choosing a setting arbitrarily.

```{r}
heavy <- sim_study("heavy", scenarios = sim_scenarios(n = 30L),
  generate = function(scenario, context) rt(scenario$n, df = 3),
  estimands = list(sim_estimand("mean", sim_truth_exact(function(scenario) 0))),
  methods = list(mean = function(data) sim_estimate("mean", mean(data))))
cal <- sim_calibrate_method(heavy,
  method = function(trim) function(data) sim_estimate("mean", mean(data, trim = trim)),
  grid = list(trim = c(0, 0.1, 0.2)), measure = "mse", replications = 50, seed = 7)
cal$best
```

## Blinded external analysis

`sim_export_blinded()` writes the data sets of a run under random codes
that reveal neither the scenario nor the replication, with the key kept
outside the export directory. Analysts return one row per code and
estimand, and `sim_external_method()` turns the rows into a method of the
study; each data set is matched by its checksum.

```{r}
dir <- tempfile("adempR-blind-")
key <- sim_export_blinded(run, dir, seed = 1)
files <- list.files(file.path(dir, "data"))
returned <- do.call(rbind, lapply(files, function(f) {
  data.frame(code = sub("\\.rds$", "", f), estimand = "mean",
             estimate = mean(readRDS(file.path(dir, "data", f)), trim = 0.1))
}))
ext <- sim_external_method(returned, paste0(dir, "-key.rds"), description = "returned by analysts")
with_ext <- sim_study("demo", scenarios = study$scenarios, generate = study$generator,
  estimands = study$estimands, methods = c(study$methods, list(external = ext)),
  measures = study$measures)
run_ext <- sim_run(with_ext, replications = 60, seed = 1, path = run$path)
s <- as.data.frame(sim_summarise(run_ext, measures = "bias"))
s[s$measure == "bias", c("scenario_id", "method", "value", "mcse")]
```

## Managing a study and its runs

`sim_fingerprint()` gives the fingerprint of a study (the hash of
everything that determines its results), `sim_protocol_export()` writes
the protocol in the ADEMP-PreReg section order, `sim_open()` opens a
stored run, and `sim_capabilities()` says which analyses the retained
outputs still allow.

```{r}
sim_fingerprint(study)
f <- tempfile(fileext = ".md")
sim_protocol_export(study, f, replications = 60)
head(readLines(f), 5)
reopened <- sim_open(run$path)
sim_capabilities(reopened)
```

## Further options of the core functions

Several capabilities are arguments of functions described elsewhere.

**Fallback values.** `sim_method(fallback = )` gives a function that is
run when every attempt of the method failed, for example an unadjusted
estimate. Its rows are stored next to the failed attempt and count only
under `sim_failure_policy(fallback = "use")`, decided at evaluation, so
the choice needs no refitting. A method with a fallback is a composite
procedure; report which policy was used.

```{r}
fragile <- sim_study("fragile", scenarios = sim_scenarios(n = 8L),
  generate = function(scenario, context) rnorm(scenario$n),
  estimands = list(sim_estimand("mean", sim_truth_exact(function(scenario) 0))),
  methods = list(trimmed = sim_method(function(data) {
    if (min(data) < -1.5) stop("outlier")
    sim_estimate("mean", mean(data, trim = 0.25))
  }, fallback = function(data) sim_estimate("mean", median(data)),
     role = "method", settings_source = "trim of 0.25 from the authors"),
  mean = sim_method(function(data) sim_estimate("mean", mean(data)), role = "benchmark")),
  measures = c("bias", "usable"),
  failure = sim_failure_policy(fallback = "use"))
run_fragile <- sim_run(fragile, replications = 40, seed = 3, path = tempfile("adempR-run-"))
s <- as.data.frame(sim_summarise(run_fragile))
s[, c("method", "measure", "value", "n_eligible")]
# replications where the fallback stood in for a failed fit
sum(sim_results(run_fragile)$estimates$used_fallback)
```

`role` marks a method as a `"benchmark"` (a comparator with known
behavior) or a `"reference"`, and `settings_source` records where its
tuning settings came from; both appear in the report.

**What a method may know.** A method sees a public view of the scenario
that holds only the fields named in `sim_method(scenario_fields = )`;
other fields (the true effect, the data-generating parameters) read as
`NULL`. Each method also gets its own copy of the data, including
`data.table` objects modified by reference, so one method cannot change
what the next one sees.

**Monte Carlo truths shared across scenarios.** With
`sim_truth_mc(factors = )`, scenarios that agree on the named fields share
one Monte Carlo truth, computed once from one stream, for example when
the truth does not depend on the sample size.

```{r}
shared <- sim_truth_mc(function(scenario, n) {
  sim_truth_value(mean(rexp(n, scenario$rate)), se = sd(rexp(n, scenario$rate)) / sqrt(n), n = n)
}, n = 1e4, factors = "rate")
```

**Large sample sanity run.** `sim_validate(large_n = )` generates one
large data set per scenario with the given overrides and runs every
method once; an estimate far from an exact or numerical truth is a
warning, which catches a method that is not consistent for the declared
estimand before the study runs.

```{r}
sim_validate(scored, large_n = list(n = 1e5), error = FALSE)
```

**Weighted summaries within levels.** With design weights,
`sim_summarise(weighted = TRUE)` adds prespecified weighted averages over
scenarios; `by` forms them within the levels of named scenario fields, so
a factor that must not be averaged over (for example an arm) is kept
apart.

```{r}
wdes <- sim_scenarios(n = c(10L, 40L), sd = c(1, 3), .weights = c(1, 3, 1, 3))
wstudy <- sim_study("weighted", scenarios = wdes, generate = study$generator,
  estimands = study$estimands, methods = study$methods["mean"], measures = "bias")
run_w <- sim_run(wstudy, replications = 30, seed = 1, path = tempfile("adempR-run-"))
w <- as.data.frame(sim_summarise(run_w, measures = "bias", weighted = TRUE, by = "sd"))
w[grepl("weighted", w$scenario_id), c("scenario_id", "measure", "value", "mcse")]
```

**Plots.** Besides the zip plot, `sim_plot()` draws estimates by method,
estimate against SE, failures, precision, runtimes, Bland-Altman
agreement between two methods and intervals by true value (including
unbounded limits).

```{r, fig.width = 6, fig.height = 4}
sim_plot(run, type = "bland_altman", methods = c("mean", "median"))
```

**Blinded reports.** `sim_report(blind_methods = TRUE)` replaces method
names, descriptions, code and fingerprints with codes, so the report can
be read before the methods are unblinded.

```{r}
f <- tempfile(fileext = ".html")
sim_report(run, f, plots = FALSE, blind_methods = TRUE, blind_seed = 1)
file.exists(f)
```

**Execution controls.** `sim_run(max_tasks = )` refuses a run that would
schedule more method fits than the budget, before anything is written;
`scenario_replications` gives some scenarios more replications than the
others (counts only increase, and every summary uses them); a run frozen
with the label `"production"` refuses changes that would supersede or
re-evaluate committed results unless `update = "production"`; and
`retry_failed = TRUE` reruns failed generations and fits with their
original streams after a fix, recording a retry round.

```{r}
try(sim_run(study, replications = 1e6, seed = 1, path = tempfile("adempR-run-"),
            max_tasks = 1000))
more <- sim_run(study, replications = 60, seed = 1, path = run$path,
                scenario_replications = c("n=10, sd=3" = 80))
reps <- sim_results(more)$replications
table(more$manifest$study$scenarios$labels[match(reps$scenario_key, more$manifest$study$scenarios$keys)])
```

**GPU methods.** A method declared with `sim_method(gpu = TRUE)` is given
one device per batch when `sim_run(gpus = )` lists device identifiers;
`CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES` holds that device while the method runs, and the
device is recorded with each attempt. Random numbers drawn on the device
are outside adempR's streams, so seed device generators from
`context$inner_seeds` and check reproducibility with `sim_verify()`.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
gpu_method <- sim_method(function(data, context) {
  # torch::torch_manual_seed(context$inner_seeds[[1]][2])
  sim_estimate("mean", mean(data))
}, gpu = TRUE)
sim_run(study, replications = 100, seed = 1, path = "gpu-run", gpus = c("0", "1"))
```
